List the Starting-Value Order of a Distance-Removal Model

Source: R/gdr_start_values.R
gdr_start_values.Rd

Read the fitted coefficient and log SD values of an unmarked distance-removal (GDR) model in the order that unmarked::gdistremoval() expects for its starts argument, with a map that names the model component and position of each value. Use it to build extra starting values for make_gdr_refitter() and fit_gdr_response_field().

Usage

gdr_start_values(model)

Arguments

model

An unmarkedFitGDR fitted by unmarked::gdistremoval() with unmarked 1.5.2, using the C or TMB engine. Its stored estimates and optimizer values must be complete and agree with each other. Models with offset() terms and zero-inflated TMB models are not supported. Finite values do not show that the model converged.

Value

A plain list:

  • starts: an unnamed numeric vector of the fitted values in starting order, on the link scales (log, logit, and log for SDs). Random-effect values are not included.

  • map: a data frame with one row per element of starts: constructor_position, the TMB parameter block (such as "beta_lambda" or "lsigma_lambda"), within_block (position in the block), fitted_position (position in the fitted optimizer vector), component ("lambda", "dist", "rem" and so on), kind ("regression" or "log_sd") and label, the coefficient or variance name stored by unmarked. For a TMB-engine model, paste block and within_block as "beta_lambda[1]" to name a start for make_gdr_refitter().

  • fitted_values: the fitted optimizer vector with its own names and order. coordinate_count is its length, not a count for AIC. random_modes_omitted gives the number of random-effect values left out in each component.

  • optimizer: the stored objective value and convergence code, as reported by the fit.

  • provider: the unmarked version, the engine and, for TMB, the TMB version. format_version identifies the layout of this list.

  • fingerprint: a SHA-256 of this list. It does not identify the data, settings or likelihood.

  • fit_eligibility_established, likelihood_evaluated and uncertainty_evaluated: always FALSE. The function only reads stored values.

Why the order matters

With the TMB engine, the order of the starts argument can differ from the order of the fitted optimizer vector. For example, unmarked may place the negative binomial dispersion after the regression and variance blocks in the starts, but next to abundance in the fitted vector. Repeated coefficient labels cannot resolve this, so the map identifies each value by its block and position and checks every value against the stored estimates.

What the function does not do

It reads stored values only. It does not evaluate the likelihood, its gradient or Hessian, and it leaves the model unchanged. A failed or nonconverged fit can still have finite values, and its stored diagnostics keep their meaning. Nonfinite or inconsistent values stop with an error rather than being dropped or repaired.

The list can be saved with saveRDS() without saving a fitted model. It cannot restore a fit. Refitting still needs the original data, transformations, formulas and optimizer settings.

See also

make_gdr_refitter(), fit_gdr_response_field(), expand_gdr_intervals()

Examples

frame <- unmarked::unmarkedFrameGDR(matrix(c(0, 0, 1, 0), 2, byrow = TRUE),
  matrix(c(0, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0), 2, byrow = TRUE),
  dist.breaks = c(0, 25, 75), unitsIn = "m", period.lengths = c(1, 2, 1))
# A fixed point for inspecting coordinates, not a converged fit.
point <- unmarked::gdistremoval(data = frame, engine = "C", K = 30,
  starts = c(log(8), log(40), qlogis(.3)), se = FALSE,
  control = list(maxit = 0))
snapshot <- gdr_start_values(point)
# Log density, log distance scale and logit removal, in starting order
snapshot$starts
#> [1]  2.0794415  3.6888795 -0.8472979
# Component, block position and stored label of each value
snapshot$map[, c("block", "within_block", "component", "kind", "label")]
#>         block within_block component       kind       label
#> 1 beta_lambda            1    lambda regression (Intercept)
#> 2   beta_dist            1      dist regression (Intercept)
#> 3    beta_rem            1       rem regression (Intercept)
